title: Tanzanian Avocado Salsa
community: Urban Tanzania — the modern fresh condiment
author: Chef Jabir
desc: Tanzanian Salsa ya Parachichi — ripe avocado mashed with tomato, onion, lemon, and coriander. The Tanzanian avocado condiment that accompanies nyama choma, pilau, and grilled fish — creamy, fresh, and completely irresistible.
longDesc: Tanzania produces excellent avocados — and Tanzanian avocado salsa is simpler and more honest than the Mexican guacamole it resembles. The tomato and coriander make it Tanzanian; the lemon keeps it bright.
steps: Halve avocados. Remove stone. Scoop flesh into a bowl.
Add lemon juice immediately — prevents browning.
Mash roughly with a fork — leave some texture.
Add tomato, onion, coriander, salt, and pepper.
chefTips: Add lemon juice immediately to prevent browning.
cookingScience: See KEN229 for avocado browning science.
sustainabilityTips: Tanzanian avocados are grown locally — zero food miles.
culturalNote: Avocado salsa represents Tanzania's modern food culture at its most confident — the same incredible avocados that the country exports to European supermarkets eaten fresh and simply at home.
